description: SB-2827 sub-plan 01 — shared behavioral oracle for the free/min/max usage-constraint procedure (dossier Rule CR-1, 'min is min, max is max, free is free'). James's canonical worked example: a surcharge of $50/unit with free_usage=3, min_usage=2, max_usage=10. Both surfaces MUST produce identical effectiveUsage for every case below: webapp `getEffectiveUsageAmount` (apps/webapp/utils/shared/quotes/qv2Formatting.ts) and addin `applyUsageConstraints` (apps/outlook-addin/src/taskpane/rfq-v2/store/rates/pricing/surchargeCalculation.ts). The drift detectors are the two app-side fixture tests — a new case block in `apps/webapp/utils/shared/quotes/__tests__/qv2Formatting.test.ts` and a new case block in the addin's `surchargeCalculation` test — both load this fixture and assert the helper's output. SCOPE — ROWS 1-10 ONLY: the dossier CR-1 procedure order is max-caps-raw -> free-reduces -> min-floors; the actual code order on BOTH surfaces is free-reduces -> min-floors -> max-caps. These two orders produce identical results for raw <= max but diverge for raw > max (e.g. raw=11 -> CR-1 yields 7, current code yields 8). Rows 1-10 are all raw <= max=10, so they are order-invariant and lock the procedure unambiguously against current code AND the canonical intent. Rows 11-12 (raw > max) and the `min > max` misconfiguration case are DEFERRED to sub-plan 07, which reorders the ONE MATH primitive set to match the dossier — see epic `sub-plan-01-followup-handoff.md` item #7. Per concern C1, every case here has min_usage > 0 (the addin's `if (minUsage > 0)` guard treats min_usage=0 as unset; min=0 cases would not exercise the floor and are not part of this oracle).
